 If you’ve been struck by how digital outrage and cultural signaling on both the left and right feel prevalent and yet simultaneously fleeting and without the backing of stable parties, there’s a term for it: hyperpolitics.
Popularized by political historian Anton Jäger, hyperpolitics helps explain how public movements today surge and then vanish without changing any underlying sources of power. What’s missing are the parties, unions, and churches that once harnessed popular energy. Jäger is the author of Hyperpolitics: Extreme Politicization Without Political Consequences. A lecturer in politics at the University of Oxford, he will sit down with FP’s Ravi Agrawal to examine the paradox of politics in major democracies.

The Gulf’s Postwar Playbook

August 11, 2026

Iran may be inching closer to a deal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, but for the other countries along the Persian Gulf, the war has permanently changed their economic and security considerations. In the 48 hours after the war began, Iran had struck every country in the Gulf Cooperation Council, upending a long-standing security bargain they held with the United States. Allison Minor, former National Security Council director for Arabian Peninsula affairs, argues that for countries in the Gulf, relying on the United States alone is no longer an option. She will join FP Live to assess how Gulf states are rethinking their security needs, their economic partnerships, and their relationship with Iran itself.

The New Rules of Economic Warfare

August 4, 2026

What do export controls between Washington and Beijing have in common with the Houthis’ ability to disrupt shipping through the Bab el-Mandeb? Both represent the embrace of chokepoints as an economic weapon. So, what tools are in this new arsenal? How are they enforced? Edward Fishman deployed these very tools during his time serving in the U.S. Defense, State, and Treasury Departments. In Chokepoints, he argues that the United States built a playbook that is now being used against it. Fishman joined FP Live to unpack what this new economic warfare costs the global economy and U.S. power.

Energy After the Shock

July 29, 2026

Oil prices are once again on the rise—and this time, they may not come down so quickly. With the Strait of Hormuz once again shut down and the Houthis attempting to block Saudi exports through the Red Sea, crude prices seem set to soar. In addition, global reservoirs of crude haven’t been restored, and China may drop its export curbs. Beyond the immediate price shock, how will countries and companies adapt their behavior in the longer term? Daniel Yergin, energy guru and economic historian who recently wrote The New Map, joined FP Live to share his insights.

Where the Iran Conflict Goes From Here

July 20, 2026

As the United States and Iran hit the escalate button once again, what will it take for both sides to pull back? One advisor the White House could have turned to was Nate Swanson, a career State Department official who served most recently as an Iran negotiator. Outside of government, he accurately predicted how Iran would respond to U.S. strikes and how it might overplay its hand after signing the memorandum of understanding. Where does Swanson see the conflict headed next?
